text: In Hobbes's variant of the Ship of Theseus, the ship reassembled from all the original planks (Ship B) has its strongest claim to be the original on the basis of which criterion?
choices: Continuous spatiotemporal history in the harbor
Functional continuity as the ship used for the annual voyage
Causal-historical continuity through gradual, uninterrupted repair
Material identity — being composed of the very same planks arranged in the same way
explanation: Ship B consists of exactly the original planks in their original arrangement, so its claim rests on material identity. The other three options — spatiotemporal, functional, and causal-historical continuity — are precisely the criteria that favor Ship A, the continuously maintained ship in the harbor. The puzzle is sharp because these criteria, normally aligned, here point to two different ships.
